advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict _precheck_code_review_applies_to to code_review project criteria that are actually ACTIVATED for the code_review gate, matching effective_criteria's activation semantics.
evidence: snapshot.py:131 `for cid, entry in gate_map.items():` iterates the RAW overlay code_review map with no activation check
snapshot.py:132-136 only skips non-`project.` ids, non-dict entries, and DET — never checks activation
overlay.py:420 `effective_criteria` = built-ins ∪ project ids whose overlay ACTIVATION opts into this review type (presence is not activation)
snapshot.py:154-160 the post-`effective_routing` loop in `_compile_gate` correctly restricts to `active` ids, but the precheck runs first and is broader
advisory.finding: _precheck_code_review_applies_to validates every raw code_review project.-prefixed non-DET overlay entry regardless of whether it is activated for the code_review gate, so a present-but-inactive code-review project LLM criterion with an empty/missing/malformed applies_to fails snapshot compile even though effective_criteria would never activate or run it.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the intended semantics for a globs list of only empty/non-string entries in select_project_applicability, and document/guard that it maps to 'ungated' rather than the prior any()-over-empty-string False.
evidence: snapshot.py:81 `real_globs = [g for g in globs if isinstance(g, str) and g]` drops empty strings
snapshot.py:82-83 `if not real_globs: return ApplicabilityDecision(applies=True, reason="ungated")` — a [""] list becomes ungated=True

registry.py (pre-change) returned `any(_glob_match(f, g) for f in changed_files for g in globs)` where globs from project_applies_to_globs kept empty strings (`[g for g in globs if isinstance(g, str)]`), so [""] would yield False
the stricter non-empty rule is only enforced for code_review LLM criteria at compile; other gates/legacy callers of select_project_applicability get no such guard
dropped.finding: select_project_applicability treats a globs list containing only empty/non-string entries (e.g. [""] or [123]) as the 'ungated' branch and returns applies=True, whereas the prior code-review consumer computed any(_glob_match(f, g) ...) over the raw string globs which would return False for an empty-string glob; on the shared legacy/plan-review path (which does NOT receive the compile-time non-empty check) this is a silent behavior change.
